reviews.verdict: Agree with the core descriptor-transport and no-path design; qualify the proof claims rather than the decision.
grounds: The implementation sends the exact borrowed descriptor returned by the opened FileBytes alongside the frame header; worker claims one OwnedFd and wraps it with the length carried in the payload.

The confined integration test reaches the actual worker, parses the document, and compares all rendered bytes against the memory route. The process probes independently pin the intended pread/stat boundary.

The protocol unit test covers missing descriptor and length/content decode. The FileBytes test covers declared lengths and short physical reads. Excess descriptors are closed by decode caller ownership/drop behavior.
ISO source constrains interpretation of PDF offsets and signed ranges, not the chosen OS mechanism or descriptor quotas. Those are owner security/performance policies.
reviews.qualification: The protocol unit test's comment says the duplicated descriptor is the same file; it actually independently opens the same path, which establishes same inode under the static fixture but does not exercise the exact same open file description. The end-to-end host test does pass the FileBytes descriptor itself, so the transport identity story is still directly supported by implementation and consumer evidence.
reviews.follow_up: Optional strengthening: add a path-unlinked-after-open control to the existing confined integration test. This would make the identity/non-reopen property observable, but the code path and current host-worker rendering test already provide substantial evidence; no PDF compliance defect is established.

reviews.verdict: No new verdict in this shard.
grounds: Signature range/digest and timestamp/revocation behavior have dedicated current review shards; this task only traced the shared FileBytes window boundary to avoid duplicating cryptographic review.

unresolved: Partial frame-header EOF is normalized to worker end-of-input whereas partial payload EOF is an error. This may be acceptable for a trusted local transport whose peer death is separately surfaced; it is a protocol robustness choice, not a PDF rule, and no separate test is proposed without a specified host-facing contract.
